timeline.say: Every film and television set runs on a fragile promise — that everyone who is called can actually do their job that day.
But sets change by the hour — weather, a delay, a location lost at short notice. And the fastest fix is often the one that quietly leaves someone behind. All-Access is built so that can't happen.
Here is a real shoot day. Salt and Light — five scenes, three locations, and every access arrangement in place. Everyone can work.
Then a storm rolls in and closes the harbour. Watch what All-Access does — live, in under a second.
Instantly, it sees everything the storm touches — every scene, every department, and every person's access needs.
The obvious fix is to move to the boatshed. It is free, and a scheduling tool would just take it. But there is no step-free way in — and someone on this crew depends on one. So All-Access refuses it.

timeline.chapter: A reason you can act on
timeline.say: And it does not just say no. It shows exactly why — the only route in has a step at the door — so a location manager can fix it. Not a vague note nobody can act on.
Instead, it offers plans that all keep every access arrangement intact — because an access need is never something to trade away for a faster day.
All-Access never decides on its own. It proposes; the people responsible approve.
Then it makes sure the new plan actually reaches every department — and it will not call the day ready until everyone has it.
All-Access. Recover any disruption — without ever leaving someone behind. For every production, and every person on it.
